capabilities: Set a local image folder (inside or outside the vault) as the workspace background
Adjust opacity, blur, size mode and blend mode of the background layer
Rotate images automatically at a fixed interval or switch manually
Shuffle playback so no image repeats within a round
Scan image headers to filter the folder by aspect ratio
extras: Desktop only (reads images through Node's fs); requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later. Not yet in the community directory; early access via BRAT. Development was AI-assisted (Doubao, DeepSeek), disclosed in the README. Makes no network requests.
motivation: The author wanted wallpaper folders of thousands of images (5,000+, tens of GB) to work without a performance cost, so only the image currently on screen is ever read into memory.
problem: Obsidian offers no built-in way to use a local image folder as an app background without hand-editing theme CSS, and loading a large wallpaper library would normally cost memory.

relations.evidence: follows vscode-background-cover, minus its particle effects, desktop pet and online gallery
The Obsidian-side layering approach was informed by obsidian-dynamic-theme-background.
the project scaffold this repository is derived from

summary: Wallpaper plugin that shows images from a local folder behind the workspace, with opacity, blur, blend modes and shuffled rotation.
